BONEHEAD launch plan

What to add next, whether to launch, and how to get the backpacker card game in front of the world.

VERDICT

Launch, as a soft launch on the web first. The game is testing well and costs almost nothing to host. What stands between it and a wider audience is depth and shareability, not polish. Build a daily reason to return and a way to share results, release quietly on the web, measure, then take it to Steam and the app stores if the numbers hold.

Where it stands

Ready for strangers

Eight tables in two rooms. Room I: classic rules, Pick Your Table, the Twins and the Pit Boss's No Weapons. Room II (opens after Room I): Madame Marrow's Open Hands, Nana's Rules, Cadaverini & Lucinda's Eye on the Card and the Ferryman's toll. Also the crypt map, bonus goals, 16 trophies, onboarding, the phone layout, iOS fixes and the skull pour.

Shipped since this plan Room II and its four rules, No Weapons, and three house rules (through Nana).

Product

What to build, in order

  1. A reason to come back every day

    A Daily Deal: everyone plays the same shuffled run that day. Finishing gives a spoiler-free result card to paste anywhere, like Wordle's grid. Add a daily leaderboard. This is the cheapest growth engine a web game has.

    Bonehead #112 · 8/8 tables · 9,202 · 🔥🔥💀

  2. House rules Started

    Every group plays Shithead differently: 7s force lower, 3s are invisible, jokers, multiples on a 10. A "Your House Rules" screen makes the game theirs, and "which rules are right?" arguments drive sharing. The engine already supports rule-change rounds, so this builds on what exists.

  3. Roguelite depth

    • About 20 trick cards instead of 6, so no two runs play alike (ideas below)
    • More opponents, each with a personality and their own twist on the rules Room II
    • Harder difficulty levels after you win, like Balatro's stakes
    • Unlockable card backs, decks and starting tricks

  4. Play with friends

    Pass-and-play on one phone is cheap and should come first. Online rooms joined by a link are the biggest feature but need a server, moderation and handling for dropouts, so build them only if the numbers justify it.

  5. Launch groundwork

    • Installable app: home-screen icon, works offline
    • Privacy-friendly analytics to see where players drop off
    • An in-game feedback link
    • A social preview image and description for shared links
    • Your own domain
    • Testing on low-end Android phones, and colour-blind-safe suits
Trick cards

Twenty tricks, three flavours

Every trick should change a decision you make, not just add points. Mix one-use tactics, build-defining passives, and a few cursed deals that pay big but bite back. Once there's a big enough pool, offer three at random after each win and let players build a strategy around them.

Launch

Three decisions first

  1. Check the name

    "Bonehead" is a common word. Search trademarks and the app stores before spending on a domain, logo or store pages.

  2. Own the Balatro comparison

    The look and chips × mult scoring are Balatro-inspired. That's legal, since game mechanics can't be copyrighted, but expect "Balatro clone" comments. Lead with what's yours: the backpacker card game everyone knows, the skull cast, and house rules.

  3. Decide what success means

    A portfolio or hobby project, a free web hit, or a paid game on Steam and mobile each need a different plan. The path below keeps all three open until the numbers decide.

How

Three phases

Phase 01–2 weeks

Get ready

Build the Daily Deal and share card, make the game installable, add analytics and a feedback link. Set up the domain and social preview image. Confirm iPad and low-end Android.

Phase 12–4 weeks

Soft launch on the web

  • itch.io and Newgrounds first: quick to publish, with players who give feedback.
  • Apply to CrazyGames and Poki, the biggest web-game sites, which share ad revenue. Poki is selective, and a finished, polished game has a real shot.
  • Go where Shithead is loved: the UK, Australia, New Zealand, the Nordics and backpackers. Post in r/playmygame, r/WebGames, r/roguelites and r/cardgames, plus UK uni and travel communities.
  • Post 10–15 second clips to TikTok and Shorts: the 10 burning the pile, the slash, a Twins win. Hook: "the backpacker card game, but it's a roguelite."
Phase 2If the numbers hold

Scale to stores

  • Open a Steam page early to collect wishlists, and bring a free demo to Steam Next Fest.
  • Ship to iOS and Android from the same code with a wrapper such as Capacitor.
  • Keep it free on the web to build an audience, and sell a premium version for $5–8 with house rules, friends mode and all unlocks.
